explanation: Spain is a famously tactile, affectionate culture — couples kissing, hugging, and holding hands in public draws little to no attention, and this applies across age groups and to same-sex couples as well. Compared to the more reserved norms in the US or parts of Northern Europe, Spaniards are generally relaxed about public affection, though it's dialed back in formal settings like a business meeting.
local_tip: Don't hold back on hand-holding, hugging, or a kiss hello/goodbye in public — it's completely normal, just default to a handshake in business settings.

also_check.note: Public affection beyond handholding is rare and can draw disapproving looks, even between married couples.
Cheek-kiss greetings are standard and couples kissing or embracing in public is common and unremarkable.
Public displays of affection between unrelated men and women are against the law and can lead to real legal consequences.

sources.title: The Economics and Social Politics of Spanish PDA
